output.best_reason: Version B has the most distinct voice and the best balance of period feel and tension. Its facts arrive through physical detail and reaction rather than recitation: the thump is "right above me," the repeater is something he "used to make us listen to," and he "sat there with my hand over my mouth." Its ending, asking the Inspector to tell Aunt Odile he was not drunk, is a human note that keeps the suspicion alive without over-explaining it. Version C is close behind, with its sardonic self-awareness and the line about loving the repeater more than the people in the house. Version E is witty and emotionally honest but slips into anachronistic phrasing ("How did that make you feel?"). Version A has strong early tension but closes with a mechanical recap of the facts, which is exactly the recited list the brief rules out. Version D is pleasant and well-paced but has the flattest texture and the least period grain.
